descriptionHtml:
Approach · OAT-02 Encryption Verification · S13 Existing spec: an email address is refused as a handoff recipient

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U4 No email or mailto that carries patient data, on any screen that shows patient data, in Hospital and in Nursing Home: no PHI is transmitted through an unencrypted path. … (UAT OAT-02 step 3; UAT OAT-02; UAT 3.3) — gate: blocked: TFA-92568 in progress
  • U5 The handoff and the task list leave the app only through the in-app Send to a signed-in RoundCompanion recipient, never to an email address (step 3 'in app only'). (UAT OAT-02 step 3; TFA-92586 AC 6; TFA-92586 AC 7; TFA-92585 AC 5) — gate: blocked: TFA-92568 in progress; TFA-92586 ready for pr; TFA-92585 ready for pr

Test design technique: Error guessing (error-guessing) — Go straight for the places most likely to break (failures, double clicks, two tabs, a wrong clock, injected instructions).

Given Two accounts

When Call handoffs.send with toUserId 'someone@example.com' (and to self, and with empty text)

Then The server refuses with 'not a RoundCompanion user', so a handoff cannot be routed out to an email address even by a crafted call

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Playwright assertion rejects.toThrow(/not a RoundCompanion user/) (step 3 'no email, in app only', enforced server-side)

Where it ran: local lane A (existing Playwright tests); test method API · API (Convex functions); lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (automated)

S13 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-02.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f, local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane A.

Test method: API · API (Convex functions); secondary: CODEREVIEW · Code review — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: matrix (lane A).

  • api/handoffs.spec.ts [api] — a handoff cannot go to yourself, to a non-account, or be empty — expected

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Lane A (Tim's api spec e2e/api/handoffs.spec.ts): it signs in the local fixture users (DEMO_USER, OTHER_USER, CONTEXT_USER) through e2e/support/backend.ts and calls handoffs.send directly; on dev nothing but Quinn may sign in, there is one shared account and no admin key, so it runs on the local …. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
